title: introduce-policy-provenance-webhook-and-kms-shadow-mapping
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Motivation:
This change introduces two complementary controls to improve auditability and reduce direct exposure of tenant CMKs in the runtime path. The goals are: attach verifiable provenance to RBAC v2 policy decisions, and limit the surface area where Customer Master Keys (CMKs) are used by introducing ephemeral 'shadow' key derivation for serving paths. This provides stronger non-repudiation in audits and a practical mitigation for attacker lateral movement where CMKs should not be present in the hot path.

High-level design:
1) Policy provenance webhook (authz/provenance-webhook):
   - A mutating/validation webhook for RBAC v2 policy objects. On policy create/update, the webhook computes a deterministic provenance fingerprint: H = sha256(policy_template || author_id || applied_region || timestamp_nonce) and stores it as policy.metadata.annotations["redwood.com/provenance-fp"].
   - The webhook also emits an evidence claim to the audit pipeline (audit/events) containing the fingerprint, policy id, author, and the KMS key identifier that signed the claim. The claim is signed with a signing key derived from the cluster KMS.
   - Validation mode can be enabled (default off) to block policies with mismatched fingerprints compared to submitted signed claims (used during rollout).

2) KMS shadow mapping (kms/shadow-mapper):
   - Introduce a lightweight service that maps long-lived tenant CMKs to short-lived derived keys used by the serving runtime. The derived key material is produced by KMS-deriveKey APIs (or HKDF) and cached per-tenant for a short TTL (configurable, default 15m).
   - Serving runtime uses the derived key id for cryptographic operations, never the tenant CMK id. Audit logs continue to record the mapping (derived -> parent CMK) in an encrypted metadata blob, persisted only to the audit store to avoid leaking CMK IDs to runtime logs.

Implementation notes and files changed (high level):
- services/authz/webhook/policy_provenance.go: webhook handler, fingerprint computation, annotation writer.
- services/authz/webhook/validation_test.go: unit tests for fingerprinting edge cases.
- services/audit/forwarder/provenance_claims.go: claim envelope builder and signer.
- services/kms/shadow_mapper/mapper.go: core mapping and cache logic, KMS integration shim.
- runtime/serving/crypto/key_provider.go: integration for consuming derived key IDs.
- ops/helm/values-security.yaml: rollout flags (validation_mode, provenance_enabled).
- docs/security/policy-provenance.md: spec and operator guide.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (default off): deploy webhook in observation-only mode (no blocking), webhook writes annotations and provenance claims to audit. Enable derived key cache in shadow-mapper but keep serving runtime configured to accept both CMK and derived key IDs.
- Phase 2: enable provenance_required for new policy creates; provide a migration tool to add annotations to existing policies and emit claims.
- Phase 3: enable validation_mode to block mismatches and flip serving runtime to prefer derived keys only.
- Rollback: helm flag provenance_enabled=false disables webhook annotation writes and proof emission; kms shadow mapping can be disabled via kms.shadow.enabled=false to revert to direct CMK usage.

Testing summary:
- Unit tests added for fingerprint determinism and annotation idempotency.
- Integration tests: webhook + audit forwarder + KMS emulator run in CI (local KMS simulator) to confirm envelope signing and verification.
- E2E smoke in canary environment validating that serving runtime can decrypt with derived keys and audit entries contain the provenance envelopes.

Security considerations:
- Evidence claims are signed with a cluster signing key stored in KMS; verification keys are available to auditors only.
- The audit store holds mapping blobs encrypted with an audit-store key to avoid exposing CMK ids in operational logs.
- Shadow-mapper caches keys only as opaque identifiers; actual key material remains within KMS or ephemeral HSM-backed buffers.

Release notes:
- New: Policy provenance webhook attaches a deterministic provenance fingerprint to RBAC v2 policy objects and emits signed evidence to the audit pipeline.
- New: KMS shadow-mapping service provides short-lived derived keys for serving runtime to reduce direct exposure of long-lived CMKs.

Manual steps for operators:
- Run scripts/docs/security/migrate_policies.sh to annotate existing policies with provenance claims.
- Update helm values in ops/helm/values-security.yaml to enable phase 1 flags in canary clusters.

Why this is different from previous residency/kms changes:
Rather than focusing on region pin enforcement or residency gating, this PR focuses on cryptographic provenance and key surface reduction. It complements region/KMS scoping work by providing verifiable audit claims and a practical runtime mitigation that avoids pushing CMKs into hot paths.

review_comments: Ethan Rios: Overall looks good. Can the provenance fingerprint include a stable policy schema version to prevent accidental drift?
Maya Thompson (author): Good point — added 'schema_version' into the fingerprinting inputs in d9a7f8c and documented the rationale.
Priya Kapoor: The audit store will now receive mapping blobs — we need to ensure retention policy hides CMK ids. Confirmed by update to audit forwarder to encrypt blobs with audit-store key.
Liam O'Connor: Make sure the shadow-mapper cache TTL is configurable per-tenant; defensive for high-churn tenants. Author responded with cache_ttl override flag and adjustable eviction in mapper.go.
Security (review): Need a threat model note for signing key compromise. Author added mitigation guidance to docs and ops checklist.
Priya Kapoor: Approving after CI green and a canary run succeeded.
merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge by Priya Kapoor (2025-09-18). Commit message consolidated to highlight provenance webhook and kms shadow mapping. Follow-up tickets created for audit retention enforcement and canary metrics (ENG-2159, ENG-2160).
release_notes: Policy provenance webhook: attach deterministic provenance fingerprints to RBAC v2 policies and emit signed evidence to audit pipeline. KMS shadow-mapping: introduce derived short-lived keys for serving to reduce CMK exposure. Rollout is opt-in via helm flags; operators should run migration tool to backfill existing policies.
